title: Union-based observation sets removed hidden-path bias at 160 shared electrical edges in two adult worm models
abstract: We tested observation designs for a direct electrical edge in passive models of two adult worm maps. A vertex cut after direct-edge removal gives a smallest extra observation set for an exact inverse-response entry. The maps had 262 and 296 retained edges. Minimum designs needed a median of two additional cells. All 1674 exact port inversions gave direct weights to numerical precision. Matched-size random sets protected 12.87 and 10.02 percent of trials. For 160 shared edges, the chosen cuts from each individual map protected only 47 and 51 in both maps. Cuts in the union protected all 160, with a median of three and at most 13 additional cells. Another 960 inversions checked these designs. This applies established graph and circuit theory. It needs passive steady dynamics, calibrated full port responses and correct support. Noise, missing bypasses and active dynamics were not tested. These are model results, not biological conductance measurements. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure and exact external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are excluded.
